title: The Substrate of Extraction
venue: MESH_ARTS, The Old American Can Factory, Brooklyn
description: Presented by UAAD at MESH_ARTS, a group exhibition exploring biological systems, industrial materials, and ecological transformation through sculpture, scent, moving image, and computational media.
introduction: Presented by UAAD at MESH_ARTS, The Substrate of Extraction brought biotechnology, sculpture, scent, moving image, and computational media into dialogue. Through cultured meat, microplastics, mealworms, and biological remains, the works examined how matter carries traces of industrial production, resource extraction, and ecological transformation. The exhibition asked what larger systems become visible when we attend to their smallest traces. Supported by the Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan; Japan Arts Council; CG-ARTS; WAN: Art & Tech Creators Global Network; and Japan Creator Support Fund.

title: Humanoid: Fall Flat
description: A playful and critical exploration of robotic failure, automation, and the gap between technological promises and lived realities, featuring artist talks, kinetic installations, live performance, and a participatory online archive.
introduction: Co-organized by UAAD and Creative Coding NYC at Hex House, *Humanoid: Fall Flat* turned robotic failures, glitches, and breakdowns into material for artistic experimentation and collective inquiry. Through kinetic installations, robotic performance, artist talks, and an interactive online archive, the program explored the gap between the promises of automation and the messy realities of machines in the physical world. Blending humor with critical reflection, the event questioned the hidden labor, infrastructures, and ideologies sustaining our increasingly automated future. The evening also featured audience voting, music, a raffle, and a community gathering celebrating four years of UAAD and three years of Creative Coding NYC.

title: ORBIT
description: A live performance showcase presented by In Motion (ITP, Tisch) and supported by UAAD, bringing movement and emerging technologies into dialogue.
introduction: Presented by In Motion (ITP, Tisch) and supported by UAAD, ORBIT brought artists, designers, engineers, and technologists together for a live performance showcase at Abrons Arts Center. Selected through an open call, the works explored how bodies, systems, and tools affect one another, treating connection as both a performance theme and a community practice.

title: (Dis)consent: A Night of Performance and Installations
description: A night of performance and interactive installations questioning how consent is negotiated across bodies, algorithms, and ecological systems.
introduction: Presented by MESH_ARTS and UAAD, (Dis)consent brought performances, interactive installations, and live generative media into dialogue. Visitors could command bodies, contribute data, alter generated images, and participate in speculative ecological systems. The program asked whether refusal, withdrawal, and renegotiation remain possible once we are already embedded in a system.

title: Worlds Adrift: UAAD x Creative Code Art
description: An evening of live A/V performances and video works tracing frequencies, ruptures, and worlds in transit.
introduction: Co-organized by Creative Code Art and UAAD, Worlds Adrift assembled artists from around the world for a temporary environment of video, sound, and live A/V performance. The works moved between geographies, languages, and natural and artificial systems, allowing images and sounds to overlap before dispersing.

title: Attention // Distraction
description: A two-day UAAD program exploring how attention is shaped and contested by digital culture, with approximately 250 visitors.
introduction: Presented by UAAD at The Blanc, Attention // Distraction examined the forces that direct our attention and the things left outside the frame. Interactive installations, net art, XR, artist-made games, algorithmic systems, live performance, and talks treated distraction as a tool for refusal, interference, and subversion.

title: FLORA Soirées
description: Four community events at FLORA HQ, with interactive installations curated by UAAD to bring artists and audiences together through shared participation.
introduction:
Across Hortus Apertus, Bacchanalia, Nexus, Inside the Studio, Amy Xiaofan Jiang, Director of UAAD, curated interactive installations for 4 FLORA’s community events. The programs brought creative practices into a social setting, inviting guests to encounter artworks through participation, conversation, and collective play.

UAAD’s role: curation of interactive installations.

title: Frankfurt Helmet + Louzhang
description: UAAD supported local promotion for Frankfurt Helmet and Louzhang-lz’s Brooklyn show, connecting the artists with New York’s modular music community and bringing UAAD community members into the audience.
introduction:
UAAD supported local promotion for Frankfurt Helmet and Louzhang-lz’s Brooklyn show, connecting their Shanghai-rooted electronic practices with New York’s modular music community. Through outreach within that scene and UAAD’s own network, UAAD helped build the audience for a sold-out night, with many UAAD community members attending.

Curated by Louzhang-lz, the program reunited two close friends with distinct audiovisual practices. Frankfurt Helmet, the duo of drummer Romna and sound artist Yufei, combines atmospheric modular synthesis with precise mechanical rhythms. Los Angeles-based musician, DJ, and film composer Louzhang-lz draws on research into ritual cultures across the Far East, connecting sounds gathered in Southwest China with contemporary electronic composition.

UAAD’s role: local promotion and community outreach.

title: Neuromantics
description: A playable Soho exhibition of artist-made games, XR, live interfaces, and moving-image works.
introduction: Co-curated with Danielle Paterson, Neuromantics turned a Soho loft into a playable ecosystem. Artists created worlds with their own rules, some open and others unlocked through collaboration, exchange, or participation. Visitors shaped what each work revealed, while evening live sets activated the space through audio interfaces and experimental sound.

introduction: An evening at NYU Tandon at The Yard exploring creative tools, resource networks, and cultural infrastructure. Presented with Artifice, Processing Foundation, and UAAD, the program brought a talk by Moon Davé together with installation and live coded performances.

title: TechnoMirage NYC
description: An in-person gathering at Index NYC exploring AI and speculative futures through conversation, a workshop, installations, and performance.
introduction: Co-organized by UAAD and Liminal at Index NYC, TechnoMirage asked what stories AI erases and how artists might reclaim them. The gathering brought panel discussion, a workshop, installations, and performance into a shared inquiry about speculative futures and creative agency.

title: connect → collide → collab
description: A cross-disciplinary gathering for sharing work in progress, meeting collaborators, and developing ideas together.
introduction:
Co-organized by Amy Xiaofan Jiang, Caren Wenqing Ye, and Aurora Zhaoqing Chen, connect → collide → collab created space for artists, designers, coders, writers, performers, and curators to share work in progress. The gathering focused on meeting potential collaborators and developing ideas together, without the pressure of a finished showcase.

Creative introductions and idea sharing were accompanied by a DJ set by Zaqi and a creative headshot session by Raven.

title: [EX UTERO] as part of ARTIFICE 004 BLACKBOX
description: A sequential new media performance at ARTIFICE 004 that staged collapse as a site of new beginnings.
introduction: The apocalypse has arrived. Final cries are swallowed in liquid ruin. Time fractures, collapses, and disappears. No origin, no inherited form. Life no longer emerges from the womb but through rupture, mutation, and synthetic gestation. [Ex Utero], Latin for "outside the womb" or "beyond the uterus," is rebirth without a blueprint—an existence forged in the breakdown of structures, where form is never fixed, only recombined. [Ex Utero] showcases six artifacts from the digital realm, each a relic of speculative realities, a fragment of mythologies still in flux, and an echo of futures that refuse to solidify. Without a singular lineage, they emerge from a landscape of continuing transformation, where species, bodies, and languages dissolve into one another. No Garden of Eden. No return to dust. The mutants only remain in the ceaseless becoming.

title: Jukebox of Dissonance: The UAAD Festival
description: A two-day festival in New York bringing together live performances, film screenings, panels, and workshops for UAAD’s second anniversary.
introduction: Organized for UAAD’s second anniversary, the New York edition of Jukebox of Dissonance brought together two days of live performances, film screenings, artist panels, and workshops. The festival created opportunities for artists and audiences to meet across disciplines and explore connections between art, technology, and collective practice. A separate virtual exhibition accompanied the festival online.

title: Transcending Boundaries
venue: Pearlona Common Room at M50, Shanghai
description: Curated by Amy Jiang in partnership with Arttoss, this Shanghai exhibition brought together 14 artists to ask what happens where one thing gives way to another. Across installation, photography, moving image and robotics, their works traced forms of contact that resist a clear dividing line.
introduction:
Boundaries are products of human thought and language. We draw them to distinguish one thing from another, to establish order and to hold a structure steady enough to govern it. A reductionist habit of thought still shapes how we understand complexity: we take a phenomenon apart as we might dismantle a machine, expecting to understand the whole by studying its components. In our minds, things begin to resemble pieces of a jigsaw puzzle. Their edges become distinct, but we lose sight of the continuities and currents that run through them.

The same lines that help us distinguish things can also keep them apart. They can arrest movement, turn conventions into rules and narrow our capacity for empathy.

What happens if we set aside those inherited definitions and look again at what we call a boundary? Its contours are neither fixed nor final. They emerge, shift and take shape again as they are crossed. Where two ecosystems meet, for instance, there is rarely a clean dividing line. There is a zone of transition, where organisms and inorganic matter act upon one another and, over time, give rise to possibilities that neither system holds alone.

Beyond the lines we draw lies fertile ground for transformation, intermingling, upheaval and new growth. The emerging artists in this exhibition approach that ground from different directions, attending to what is fluid, ambiguous, multiple or provocative, and to what still eludes our language and perception.

Curated by Amy Jiang in partnership with Arttoss.

title: TechnoMirage: Creative AI Futures
description: An online conversation with Parsons on authorship, ethics, access, and creative agency in AI.
introduction: Presented by UAAD and Parsons School of Design Strategies, this online edition of TechnoMirage brought artists, designers, and technologists into a conversation about creative AI. Panelists discussed authorship, ethics, access, and how AI reshapes collaboration and creative labor.

title: Ghosts in the Feedback Loop
description: An immersive virtual exhibition exploring how people erased or distorted by algorithms can reclaim technological space.
introduction: In the feedback loops of machine learning, certain bodies, cultures, and ways of knowing are made visible, distorted, or erased. Like ghosts—excluded yet ever-present—they haunt the machine. They slip through algorithmic blind spots, bend systems’ logic, and disrupt with glitches and ruptures that unsettle computational control. But ghosts don’t just haunt—they rewire. They assert presence, reframe meaning, and speak in forms the system was never trained to understand. Through cracks in the loop, they reemerge as designers of new imaginaries for themselves and for the communities the system failed to see.

description: A public panel on AI, ethics, and creative practice presented with Parsons School of Design.
introduction: Presented by Parsons School of Design and UAAD as part of the Design with AI course, this panel brought artists, designers, educators, and researchers into dialogue about how AI reshapes artistic practice and the ethical questions that follow.

title: Jukebox of Dissonance: The Virtual Exhibition
description: A virtual exhibition presented as part of Jukebox of Dissonance, marking UAAD’s second anniversary.
introduction: Presented as part of Jukebox of Dissonance for UAAD’s second anniversary, this virtual exhibition brought artists working across disciplines into a shared online space. The exhibition formed the online edition of the program, alongside a separate festival in New York.

title: Care is Art, Art is Care
description: A virtual exhibition curated by Joana Alarcão, with an immersive world developed by UAAD, exploring care across ecological, personal, and collective life.
introduction:
Curated by Joana Alarcão with an immersive virtual world developed by UAAD, Care is Art, Art is Care explores artistic practice as a way of caring for environments, communities, and ourselves.

The exhibition connects environmental stewardship with personal relationships, identity, mental health, and resilience. Its three sections consider ecological care, inner and relational experience, and the challenges of sustaining well-being. Together, the works question ideals of self-sufficiency and foreground the interdependence of human and more-than-human life.

The exhibition is a collaboration between Insights of an Eco Artist and UAAD. UAAD’s role: immersive virtual world development.

title: Matrix of the Not-Yet
description: An interactive web-based curatorial project mapping possible worlds across social, technological, and ecological intersections.
introduction: An interactive publication featuring 19 artist groups. Inspired by the rhizome, Matrix of the Not-Yet replaces a linear reading path with a decentralized network of visions for possible futures.

title: Unbound Variable
description: A virtual exhibition by UAAD and Not Yet Arts examining the contested boundaries between technology, nature, and human identity.
introduction:
Organized by Not Yet Arts and UAAD, Unbound Variable explores the fluid boundaries between art and life in an increasingly hybrid world. The exhibition brings technology, nature, and human identity into dialogue through digital installations, bio-art, and ecological interventions.

Responding to technological acceleration and ecological crisis, the works examine the interdependence of organic and synthetic worlds while questioning systems that commodify nature and data. They invite a more-than-human perspective and challenge inherited divisions between natural and artificial, human and non-human, subject and object.

Together, the works ask how artistic practice can reconsider colonial, patriarchal, and capitalist structures that sustain these divisions.

title: Alt-Alterity: An Immersive Virtual Exhibition
description: A virtual exhibition featuring 26 artist groups from 13 countries, exploring alternative forms of identity and relation.
introduction: In the midst of gathering storms — genocides, wars, forced displacements, global climate collapse, the ascendency of technocracy, alongside the unyielding presence of unjust ideologies such as sexism, racism, colonialism, imperialism, and capitalism — emerges our curatorial and editorial initiative, Alt-Alterity. It stands as an attempt to provoke a co-imagination of an alternative paradigm for how we, as humans, engage with both the “other” inhabitants of our planet and “each other” within our societies.

title: Ties That Cannot Be Unbound
description: A virtual exhibition reconsidering our relationships with living and non-living entities.
introduction: Our lives are shaped by the ties that bind us to the world around us. These ties weave networks of relationships that make up our narratives and help us navigate the complexities of our planet. UAAD invites you to explore these connections with Ties That Cannot Be Unbound, an online exhibition that discusses the interconnectedness of spirituality and physicality, the blurred boundaries between the living and the non-living, and the ties between our bodies and the environment. Featuring outstanding works in sound, image, film, and interaction, this exhibition responds to the question: what kinds of ties are impossible to unbind? Join us on a journey of self-discovery and collective action towards a more sustainable and harmonious future.
